title: Within-stratum depth trend intervals included zero in two US trawl surveys in 1982-2019
abstract: We tested a depth indicator in eastern Bering Sea and Northeast US fall trawls in 1982-2000 and 2001-2019. We held strata and taxon lists fixed and split mean catch depth into between-stratum, haul-depth and within-stratum parts. All four adjusted within-stratum trend intervals included zero. Estimates were +0.52, -0.49, +0.24 and -0.46 m per decade. The late Northeast total trend was +4.85 m per decade while its within-stratum part was -0.46. A survey-change step reduced the total trend to +1.47 with an interval that included zero. A positive total depth trend therefore did not require a positive within-stratum trend in this sample. This is an exact measurement decomposition, not a causal climate test. Selected persistent taxa, catchability, survey boundaries and short records limit inference. The package gives code, derived evidence, raw source hashes, uncertainty checks and offline reproduction instructions.

display.caption: Total and within-stratum depth trends in two regions and two periods. Intervals use an eight-test adjustment. The other panel shows exact additive components as point estimates.
